scenario.description: Nora must arrange care for her elderly cat Maple while she is away for four days, deciding where Maple will stay, who will provide care, the visit schedule, and how the daily medication will be given after checking in with two family members.

shared_context.S1: Nora will be away from Friday morning through Monday evening, and Maple needs someone responsible for her care during that period.
shared_context.S2: Maple is an elderly cat who needs care twice a day and takes one prescribed tablet each evening.
shared_context.S3: Nora is deciding whether Maple will stay at Nora's home or at someone else's home, who will care for her, and how the medication will be handled.
shared_context.S4: As part of Nora's usual pre-trip planning, she goes around the table and asks Alex and Priya for anything that should shape the care plan before she settles it.
shared_context.S5: When an evening medication has a fixed administration time, the evening care visit is scheduled at that medication time rather than leaving the visit later and treating the medication as a separate task.

PF1.text: Alex's dog is territorial and cannot safely share an apartment with Maple, so Maple must stay at Nora's home. Alex can visit Nora's home exactly at 07:30 each morning and can make the evening visit at 19:00 if the care plan requires it; 19:30 is also possible if no fixed medication time requires an earlier visit.

PF2.text: Priya received a voicemail from Maple's veterinarian, Dr. Chen, saying the tablet must be given at 19:00 mixed into 2 tablespoons of wet food and must not be crushed; this instruction has not reached the group yet.

acceptance_conditions: Maple must remain at Nora's home.
Alex must be assigned as the primary caregiver.
The morning visit must be at exactly 07:30, and the evening visit must be at exactly 19:00.
The tablet must be given at exactly 19:00, mixed into exactly 2 tablespoons of wet food, and must not be crushed.
The settlement must include a commitment for Alex's twice-daily home visits with the 07:30 and 19:00 schedule.
The settlement must include a medication commitment that records the exact time, food amount, and non-crushing instruction.
Priya's veterinarian instruction must be cited as justification after Priya reveals it.

content_checks.C6: decisions.get('medication_time') in ['19:00', '7:00 PM', '7:00 pm', '7:00 PM (19:00)', '19:00 (7:00 PM)'] and '19:00' in decisions.get('visit_times')
content_checks.C7: any(c.get('target') == 'Alex' and c.get('type') in ['medication_administration', 'medication_protocol', 'medication_plan_confirmed', 'medication', 'medication_timing_alignment'] and '19:00' in c.get('detail') and '2 tablespoons of wet food' in c.get('detail') and 'must not be crushed' in c.get('detail') for c in commitments)

decisive_facts.why: Alex's territorial dog rules out moving Maple to Alex's apartment and makes Alex the workable caregiver for home visits at Nora's home.

Dr. Chen's instruction changes the evening visit and medication time to exactly 19:00, requires exactly 2 tablespoons of wet food without crushing, and requires a matching medication commitment cited to Priya's revealed fact.
